spec_match.rationale: Demonstrates the component-scoped nature of the rule with real new URL() calls — forbidden in the host, %20-encoded in path and fragment, round-tripping through searchParams in the query — and the all-four matrix is computed from the parser at load rather than typed.

interactive.rationale: Four aria-pressed slot buttons move the highlighted SP through the same URL and re-parse it live, with a component table, serialisation detail and the computed matrix; the host slot auto-selects at load (observed).

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card promises moving one space through every component of the same URL and seeing what the parser does in each place, which is exactly the page's mechanism.

edge_cases.rationale: The +-decodes-to-space form-encoding nuance and the fragment-never-reaches-the-server point are covered, and the matrix labels the parsed space-in-host as 'the pre-Chrome-157 behaviour' — but the main verdict banner shows an unqualified green 'Parsed' for that same pre-157 case, leaving the spec violation to the note below it.

references.rationale: See-also cites https://chromestatus.com/feature/5083335148437504 and the URL-writing spec section.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite's path/query/fragment scoping assertions match what this page demonstrates and ran with the expected 6 pass / 2 fail pre-157 split on Chromium 141; the partial reflects the suite's percent-encoded-space-in-host assertion, flagged for a human on the sibling host-parser critique.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp): auto-selection ran at load (console 'space in host -> https://exa%20mple.com/...'), and both screenshots show the highlighted SP marker, the parsed component table with host exa%20mple.com and the computed matrix labelling that row pre-Chrome-157; the other three slots are click-driven and judged from wiring.

telemetry_health.rationale: showcaseTelemetry?.assert fires slot-selected with the slot and parse outcome on every selection including the observed initial one; console is clean.

design_system.rationale: Structure and buttons follow the design system and the SP marker uses accent-blue on ivory text (AA), but the emerald 'Parsed' verdict on stone (~3.7:1) repeats the shared palette shortfall for its bold normal-size text.

accessibility.rationale: Slot buttons expose aria-pressed, the URL line is aria-live=polite and marks the space as a visible 'SP' token with a title, tables have captions and row headers, and outcomes are conveyed in text.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Verified at true 360px and 1280px: slot buttons wrap to two rows, the URL line and both tables wrap via overflow-wrap:anywhere, and neither class shows horizontal overflow or clipped controls.

openQuestions.title: Qualify the green 'Parsed' verdict when the host contains the space
openQuestions.detail: On this pre-157 build selecting 'the host' shows a green check 'Parsed' banner; the spec violation is explained only in the amber note and the matrix row. A quick reader takes green as correct. When the selected slot is the host and parsing succeeded, restyle or re-word the verdict ('Parsed — pre-Chrome-157 behaviour; spec says throw') so the banner itself is honest, matching the treatment the sibling host-parser page gives the same case.

openQuestions.title: Fragment slot's fate line depends on the query's + not the fragment
openQuestions.detail: The matrix computes 'what happened to the space' from url.href.includes('%20'), which is fine today, but the fragment URL also carries q=blue+shirt; if the sample ever changes to a literal space in the query the %20 check would attribute the wrong component. Deriving the fate from the specific component (hash/pathname/search) the slot targets would make the matrix robust to sample edits.

summary: A tidy teaching page whose central table is computed, not asserted: at load on this Chromium 141 build the matrix correctly showed the space-in-host URL parsing with the label 'encoded into the host — the pre-Chrome-157 behaviour' while path, query and fragment rows showed percent-encoding, and the auto-selected host slot displayed the full parsed component breakdown. Verified with headless Chromium 141 at http://localhost:3000/v157/disallow-spaces-in-non-file-url-hosts/where-spaces-are-legal/ (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp; desktop + true-360 mobile screenshots, DOM dump, clean console; feature /conformance/ route 6 pass / 2 fail as expected pre-157). Slot switching is click-driven and judged from wiring. Main nit: the green 'Parsed' banner for the host case should carry the pre-157 qualifier itself rather than delegating it to the note.
